fusion_ranked_evidence.title: Supreme Court Case Could Strip Medicaid of Crucial Civil Rights | Commonwealth Fund
fusion_ranked_evidence.snippet: # An Upcoming Supreme Court Case Could Strip Medicaid Beneficiaries and Safety-Net Providers of Crucial Civil Rights. On November 8, the Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether Section 1983 of the Civil Rights Act grants Medicaid beneficiaries and providers the right to sue states that violate their coverage and payment rights. For more than 50 years, Medicaid beneficiaries and providers have been able to seek protection from the federal courts when state officials violate their coverage and payment rights. The right to access the court comes from section 1983 of the Civil Rights Act of 1871, which grants people the ability to turn to the federal courts when states violate rights guaranteed by law, including the right to Medicaid services. In *Talevski*, the Court has decided to more broadly consider whether section 1983’s right of access to federal courts will remain for beneficiaries and providers who claim that state officials have violated rights guaranteed under Medicaid, and not just for Medicaid nursing homes.
